title: Contract Architecture, Drafting Precision, Transparent Review, and Negotiation Reasoning Library
scope_note: Usable source-grounded checkpoint. Full embedded text was extracted and the contents inventoried, but only cited sections received substantive review. Do not infer complete book processing.

data_model.unknown_values: Use null plus an explanation in transaction-specific JSON; use marked placeholders in drafts.

records.title: Stark’s transaction-concept framework
records.primary_question: Which deal concept best expresses the business term?

content.source_scope: Stark presents these as distinct contract-building concepts used to translate a deal into provisions.

limitations: Source framework only; not a universal legal taxonomy.

records.title: Adams’s language-function categories
records.primary_question: What function does the wording perform?

content.source_scope: Adams organizes language by function and discusses how conditions may be expressed through such categories.

records.title: Stark’s condition-and-obligation framework
records.primary_question: What duty is triggered by which event?

content.source_rule: Analyze a condition and the obligation it triggers as separate elements; identify the party, trigger, duty, and consequence of nonoccurrence.

records.title: Adams’s condition-signaling analysis
records.primary_question: Does the wording clearly mark the intended condition?

content.source_rule: Inspect sentence structure and language function; do not rely on a modal verb alone to make an obligation operate as a condition.

records.title: Stark’s representation and warranty framework
records.primary_question: What factual assurance, promise, and remedy are in the deal?

content.source_rule: Stark distinguishes representation and warranty roles in its transaction and remedy analysis and uses the wording to discuss risk allocation.

limitations: The cited source’s U.S.-law discussion is not current-law verification.

records.title: Adams’s fact-statement wording recommendation
records.primary_question: Are labels being used to decide a remedy without an express term?

content.source_rule: Adams critiques relying on represents/warrants labels to settle remedies and recommends plain fact-statement wording with remedies stated directly when needed.

limitations: The book’s legal discussion and authorities were not independently verified.

records.title: Stark’s definition-as-standard analysis
records.primary_question: Does the definition change scope, rights, duties, or risk?

content.source_rule: Treat a definition as a transaction standard when its breadth changes the parties’ position; check each use.

records.title: Adams’s defined-term language checks
records.primary_question: Does the defined term stay clear and useful across its uses?

content.source_rule: Check for circularity, overlap, unnecessary terms, and consistency between a definition and every provision that uses it.

records.title: Adams’s attachment-incorporation recommendation
records.primary_question: Does the agreement identify each attachment and state its intended role?

content.source_rule: Adams generally recommends relying on the body’s specific reference to an attachment rather than adding a blanket statement that every attachment is part of the contract; the source identifies a master-agreement schedule exception.

limitations: The recommendation is not a conclusion about legal incorporation in a particular jurisdiction.

records.title: Stark’s transaction document architecture
records.primary_question: Are the business provisions, endgame, schedules, and exhibits organized for the transaction?

content.source_rule: Use contract parts and transaction chronology to organize provisions; action, endgame, schedules, and exhibits serve distinct roles.

records.title: Adams’s document layout and sequence guidance
records.primary_question: Can readers find and follow related provisions?

content.source_rule: Use consistent sections, sequence, and list structure to support navigation and readability.

records.title: Keep contract concepts and language functions separate
records.primary_question: What is the provision doing in the deal, and how is that function expressed?

content.mapping_rule: Record the transaction concept and the language function separately. Do not assume a one-to-one mapping or treat the two lists as interchangeable.
use_steps: Identify the party, action or fact, object, scope, trigger, timing, exceptions, and consequence.
Record gaps between the intended consequence and the words used.

records.title: Translate agreed deal points into provisions
records.primary_question: What agreed term must the contract express?

steps: List agreed business terms and source documents.
Separate confirmed, proposed, disputed, unknown, and not applicable points.
Translate each point into the applicable contract concept.
Organize provisions and identify dependent terms.
do_not_infer: acceptance from an offer or draft
money, deadlines, ownership shares, liability limits, or rates
consent or approval that was not supplied

applicability_conditions: A business term, instruction, or source document is supplied.
limitations: A preliminary draft may proceed with marked gaps; unknown terms stay unknown.

records.title: Separate conditions from promises
records.primary_question: Does the clause state a duty, a condition to a duty, or both?

content.rule: Identify the condition and the obligation independently. Check whether the contract states who owes what if the condition is satisfied and what happens if it is not. Do not label failure of a condition as breach without further analysis.
content.business_choice: Changing an obligation into a condition can change who bears the risk of nonoccurrence; expose that choice.

limitations: The source books describe legal consequences that require jurisdiction-specific verification.

records.title: Preserve the representation and warranty drafting difference
records.primary_question: Do the parties intend a factual assertion, a promise, or a specified remedy for an inaccurate fact?

content.stark_position: Stark’s framework distinguishes representations and warranties and uses the distinction in discussing remedies and risk allocation.
content.adams_position: Adams critiques reliance on represents/warrants labels to settle remedies and recommends introducing facts plainly and addressing remedies directly when needed.
content.library_rule: Show both source positions. For a live agreement, state the factual proposition, intended remedy or remedy exclusion, and any negotiated label choice separately; flag current-law verification. No automatic house-style winner.
content.example_classification: The books’ hypotheticals, competing formulations, and reported legal commentary are teaching material, not independently verified authority.

limitations: No current law or jurisdiction has been verified.

records.title: Check definitions for scope and operation
records.primary_question: Does every defined term mean what the parties intend wherever it appears?

checks: Compare each definition with the supplied deal scope.
Search every occurrence and read the surrounding provision.
Check for circularity, overlapping terms, inconsistency, unused terms, and key words whose scope expands unrelated assets.
Treat a definition that changes a right, duty, standard, or risk allocation as substantive.
content.change_classification: Narrowing or broadening a definition can change commercial scope; do not call it editorial without checking effect.

records.title: Map contract parts and missing attachments
records.primary_question: Does the contract structure make the bargain, dependencies, schedules, and exhibits complete and easy to follow?

review: Identify preamble, recitals, operative sections, definitions, schedules, exhibits, signature blocks, and endgame.
Group related provisions and inspect cross-references.
Confirm each referenced schedule or exhibit is present, versioned, and consistent with the body.
Distinguish factual schedules from attached agreement forms and other exhibits.
content.source_difference: Stark discusses using the definition or interpretive section to address attachment status; Adams generally advises against a blanket attachment-is-part clause when the body specifically references the attachment, subject to a master-agreement exception. Keep this source difference visible.
content.library_rule: Inspect exact references, the Agreement definition, precedence language, and the attachment structure. Do not add or remove a blanket incorporation sentence without recording the commercial and legal choice.
content.missing_document_action: Name the missing item and explain which provision cannot be fully evaluated without it; do not assume its contents.

records.title: Review in layers, then trace provisions together
records.primary_question: What does each provision do for the parties commercially, operationally, and legally?

sequence: Identify version, user role, review objective, and related documents.
Check payment, exit, and key business terms.
Read the whole contract, including definitions and schedules.
Prepare prioritized findings and traceable changes.

records.title: Assess risk, control, and standards separately
records.primary_question: Who bears the risk, who controls the relevant event, and what standard decides performance?

questions: What risk does the wording allocate?
How likely is the risk and what would its consequence be?
Can the obligated party control the outcome?
Who decides whether a standard is met?
Would a more specific standard help, or is flexibility part of the bargain?
What mitigation is agreed, and what does it cost?
content.reporting_rule: Explain commercial allocation without assuming an unfavorable term is unclear, invalid, or unreasonable. Do not compress risk, legal enforceability, and drafting clarity into one score.

limitations: Risk probability and value require supplied facts; legal enforceability requires separate authority.

records.title: Name the mechanism of uncertain meaning
records.primary_question: Is the problem ambiguity, insufficient specificity, conflict, omission, vagueness, or a combination?

mechanisms.ambiguity: Two or more inconsistent readings are plausible.
mechanisms.insufficient_specificity: A broad expression leaves the intended boundary or measurement unstated.
mechanisms.conflict: Two contract components do not fit together.
mechanisms.omission: A material issue is not addressed.
mechanisms.vagueness: A context-dependent standard leaves room for disagreement.

content.repair_rule: For each plausible reading, state what changes. If repair selects one reading or fills a missing business choice, classify it as substantive or choice-dependent.

limitations: These categories can overlap; the source treats their boundaries as blurred.

records.title: Use a consistent and precise language profile
records.primary_question: Would this edit improve clarity without changing the negotiated result?

profile: Remove redundancy only after checking that it is not a qualification, limitation, or useful repetition.
Keep defined and legal terminology consistent.
Restructure long or ambiguous sentences only after mapping actor, action, trigger, exception, and consequence.
Use formatting to make lists and conditions readable.
content.change_boundary: A clearer sentence that changes who acts, when, on what standard, or with what exception is substantive.

limitations: Editorial profile is not binding law and yields to the parties’ agreed wording when the style change is immaterial.

records.title: Anchor dates and periods to actual events
records.primary_question: What event starts the period, does it run forward or backward, and when does it end?

review: Identify the triggering event and the party that knows it occurred.
State the direction and unit of time.
Check whether a point in time or a duration is intended.
Inspect expressions whose direction can be unclear.
Do not calculate a date without the relevant date, business-day rule, time zone, and calendar inputs.

limitations: The source discusses time-counting conventions and case examples; this library does not certify them as current law.

records.title: Test payment formulas and ranges at boundaries
records.primary_question: Can a reader calculate what is due at every relevant value and boundary?

review: State the calculation inputs, units, timing, and rate structure.
Decide whether tiers are incremental or one rate applies to the whole quantity.
Check every adjacent range for gaps and overlaps, including fractional values.
Use equations or a sample calculation only when they clarify the negotiated formula.
Run boundary examples at the first value, each transition, and the last value.

limitations: Do not supply amounts or rates absent from the deal terms.

records.title: Trace termination, payment, remedies, and survival as events
records.primary_question: What happens at each exit or default event, and what duties continue afterward?

event_map: post-termination return, access, payment, and survival
checks: Identify the trigger, decision-maker, notice, cure period, consequence, effective date, and related provision.
Check whether monetary remedies, caps, exclusions, indemnities, and survival clauses interact.
Confirm which duties survive and for how long.
Do not assume general language resolves a specific conflict or that every duty survives.

limitations: Contract consistency does not establish enforceability.

records.title: Collect and classify the deal facts
records.primary_question: What facts or choices materially affect the requested draft or review?

fields: transaction and covered assets or services
related agreements, schedules, amendments, incorporated documents
content.drafting_behavior: Ask only decision-critical questions; proceed with a clearly marked preliminary draft when useful; keep JSON unknowns null with an explanation.

records.title: Make every proposed change traceable
records.primary_question: What exactly changes and who benefits or takes on a new burden?

content.priority_rule: Offer the smallest change that addresses the identified issue before a full rewrite.

records.title: Explain what the contract says and support informed negotiation
records.primary_question: Can each party understand duties, rights, money, approvals, failure consequences, exit, and unresolved points?

guardrails: Do not call a term standard without evidence.
Explain asymmetry and a plausible commercial interest without inventing motive.
Keep explanation outside operative text unless requested.

records.title: Use specialist modules only when the deal calls for them
records.primary_question: Does the transaction involve confidentiality, freelance technical services, or music/creative work?

confidentiality: lawful reporting and protected disclosure review
technical_services: background tools and newly created work
music_creative: ownership, administration, permission, credit, royalties, cash compensation
music_preferences: For composition/songwriting/publishing-only agreements, do not expand scope to masters, stems, DAW sessions, production files, branding, artwork, or unrelated assets absent express agreement.

Distinguish private portfolio use from public posting, public credit, advertising, licensing, sale, and other public uses. User preference: allow appropriate private portfolio presentation; require prior approval for public use. This is not a legal default.
Do not treat payment, role labels, or work-made-for-hire wording alone as settling ownership. Route to current copyright authority and qualified counsel.
content.storage_rule: Keep actual parties, works, rates, percentages, ownership shares, and approvals out of reusable records.

limitations: User-directed checklists only; no legal conclusion or default clause.

records.title: Route legal conclusions to current authority
records.primary_question: What jurisdiction, date, contract context, and legal proposition would need verification?

content.library_status: No legal authority was independently checked for this library. Book passages and their cited cases are not treated as current verified law.
content.safe_output: Continue useful issue spotting and drafting analysis; state what remains unverified and when qualified counsel is needed.

claim_ledger.proposition: Stark presents seven transaction-concept categories—representations, warranties, covenants, rights, conditions, discretionary authority, and declarations—and treats selection among them as translating agreed business terms into contract provisions.
qualifications: This is Stark’s pedagogical framework, not a claim that every jurisdiction uses identical labels or consequences.
verification_needed: Verify relevant legal effect in the governing jurisdiction when a provision depends on it.

claim_ledger.proposition: Adams organizes contract wording by language function and treats conditions as a subject expressed through language categories, rather than as an additional one-to-one member of Stark’s seven transaction concepts.
qualifications: Paraphrases the organization of the cited sections; it does not reproduce the full taxonomy.

claim_ledger.proposition: The two books use related but non-equivalent taxonomies: keep transaction-concept classification and language-function classification in separate fields, then map them for a particular provision.
qualifications: Editorial synthesis, not either author’s term.

claim_ledger.proposition: Stark’s drafting workflow starts from the agreed business terms, identifies the contract concepts needed to express them, and organizes the resulting provisions.
qualifications: Applied as a drafting-analysis workflow, not as a legal rule.

claim_ledger.proposition: Stark distinguishes a condition to an obligation from the obligation itself and advises identifying the event that triggers the duty, the obligated party, and what follows if the condition is not satisfied.
qualifications: The book’s explanations of common-law consequences are not independently verified or assumed applicable.
verification_needed: Verify condition doctrine and consequences under governing law.

claim_ledger.proposition: Adams analyzes how the wording and structure signal conditions and warns against relying on a modal verb alone where the intended effect is conditional.
qualifications: The source discusses several formulations; do not apply one mechanically without checking the intended consequence.

claim_ledger.proposition: Stark treats representations as fact statements and warranties as promises associated with specified remedies in the book’s U.S.-law discussion; it uses the distinction to analyze risk allocation.
qualifications: This is a source report of a 2013 text’s framework and legal discussion, not a current-law conclusion.
verification_needed: Identify transaction, governing law, and remedies before relying on this distinction.

claim_ledger.proposition: Adams discusses the labels represents and warrants as terminology for fact statements, critiques treating those verbs as a dependable remedy selector, and recommends plain fact-statement wording with remedies addressed directly when needed.
qualifications: Adams’s recommendation and its legal analysis are reported as source positions; cited authorities were not independently checked.
verification_needed: Verify the intended cause of action and remedy under governing law.

claim_ledger.proposition: The books materially differ on the drafting significance of representation/warranty labels: Stark’s framework assigns distinct remedy-related roles, while Adams disputes relying on those words to determine remedies. Preserve both positions and expose the choice.
qualifications: The source disagreement is editorial/legal-theory context; neither book is current legal authority for a specific transaction.
verification_needed: Current primary authority and qualified counsel for the jurisdiction and transaction.

claim_ledger.proposition: Stark treats definitions as strategic standards that can change rights, duties, and risk allocation; review each term in its uses.
qualifications: A source-grounded drafting and transaction-analysis point, not an enforceability conclusion.

claim_ledger.proposition: Adams explains that defined terms can aid consistency but can also obscure meaning through circularity, overlap, or unnecessary defined terms; inspect each use.
qualifications: Summarizes selected sections only.

claim_ledger.proposition: Stark organizes provisions around transaction content, key action sections, endgame provisions, and schedules or exhibits; organization depends on the transaction.
qualifications: Source guidance is a drafting model, not a mandatory sequence.

claim_ledger.proposition: Adams addresses section organization and sequencing, reader navigation, and list formatting; its layout recommendations are a style profile, not binding law.
Stark distinguishes schedules used for information or exceptions from exhibits used for related documents or forms and emphasizes checking that listed attachments exist and are complete.
qualifications: Paraphrase of textbook treatment; whether incorporation is effective depends on text and law.
verification_needed: Verify the operative text and applicable incorporation rules if legal effect matters.

claim_ledger.proposition: Adams generally treats a contract’s specific reference to an attachment as sufficient to bring it within the contract and advises against a redundant blanket statement, while recognizing a master-agreement schedule exception.
qualifications: This is the author’s drafting recommendation; effectiveness under governing law was not independently checked.
verification_needed: Verify incorporation effect under governing law and inspect the specific attachment structure.

claim_ledger.proposition: Stark’s review framework examines business purpose, fit with the agreed deal, client interests, legal and drafting questions, practical effects, and interactions with other provisions; it also recommends reading key business terms and then the whole agreement.
qualifications: The library adds user-requested factual, operational, and source-traceability fields.

claim_ledger.proposition: Stark frames risk review around identifying and assessing risk, client risk tolerance, control over promised outcomes, the selected standard, and possible mitigation.
qualifications: Do not turn this into an aggregate contract-quality score or a default preference for the most aggressive position.

claim_ledger.proposition: Adams distinguishes ambiguity, insufficient specificity, conflict, omitted issues, and vagueness as different sources of uncertain meaning; the repair depends on the mechanism.
qualifications: The boundaries can overlap; source itself discusses blurred boundaries.

claim_ledger.proposition: Adams identifies time wording as a source of uncertainty and recommends making the intended starting point, direction, and reference time clear.
qualifications: The book discusses conventions and case examples that are not independently checked; do not calculate dates without supplied inputs.
verification_needed: Check agreed dates, definitions, calendar rules, time zones, and current governing law where relevant.

claim_ledger.proposition: Adams flags ambiguity in rate structures and gaps or overlaps in numerical ranges; complex formulas may be clearer as equations with defined variables and checked examples.
qualifications: Illustrations are source examples and are not reused as transaction terms.

claim_ledger.proposition: Adams’s language guidance prioritizes clarity, precision, consistency, avoiding redundancy, and keeping sentence structure readable.
qualifications: Apply only when the edit preserves conditions, exceptions, limitations, and the intended business outcome.

claim_ledger.proposition: The user requires deal facts to be classified as confirmed, proposed, disputed, unknown, or not applicable; unresolved terms use null in JSON and marked placeholders in drafts.
The user requires each finding to preserve the original contract text, identify its type and effect, show parties affected, alternatives, missing facts, priority, and legal-review triggers.
The user requires every revision to be classified by its substantive effect and to show original text, proposed text, reason, expected effect, related provisions, and unresolved choices.

The user requires plain-language explanations and negotiation options that separate preferred positions, alternatives, tradeoffs, and counsel questions without calling terms standard without evidence.
The NDA, freelance technical-service, and music/creative modules are user-directed application preferences subordinate to the general library; they are not legal defaults or book-derived rules.
The user requires current-law claims to be separately verified by primary or official sources for a specified jurisdiction and requires unknown legal issues to remain unverified.
The user requires synthetic tests for the listed contract-review failure modes; results measure disciplined issue spotting, not court outcomes.
